fact: 1900年义和团运动期间，满洲的义和团攻击在建的中东铁路；俄国以保护铁路投资为名向满洲出动17万军队并占领战略要地，大英百科全书称此事引起日本对俄国意图的警惕，俄国对满洲的占领直接导向1904—1905年日俄战争。

sources.title: Trans-Siberian Railroad | History, Map, Geography, & Facts | Britannica
sources.quote: In 1900 the Boxer Rebellion took place in China, targeting "foreign devils" and seeking to drive them out. Rebels in Manchuria had a specific grievance against the railroad, which they believed was responsible for upsetting the harmony of the region and causing droughts and flooding. The Russians moved 170,000 troops into Manchuria to protect their investment there, raising alarm in Japan over Russian intentions.

sources.title: Resistance Against Russia in Manchuria (1900) | Whence We Came (philas.org.au)
sources.quote: Other Russian troops advanced along the CER tracks under construction which the Boxers were trying to destroy. The troops seized all strategic points in Manchuria. The Russian occupation of Manchuria led directly to the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-5.

fact: 西伯利亚大铁路采用分段同时建设：西西伯利亚段（车里雅宾斯克至鄂毕河）1896年完工，中西伯利亚段（鄂毕河至伊尔库茨克）1899年完工；到1901年初全线仅余约2000公里未建成，因气候与地质条件改经满洲修筑的中东铁路于1903年投入运营，贝加尔湖在1905年环湖铁路通车前仍须轮渡接驳客货。

sources.title: Trans-Siberian Railroad | History, Map, Geography, & Facts | Britannica
sources.quote: The first stretch was the West Siberian Railroad from Chelyabinsk to the Ob River, completed in 1896. The second stretch, the Central Siberian Railroad, was from the Ob River to Irkutsk on the western shore of Lake Baikal; it was completed in 1899. ... By early 1901 only about 1,240 miles (2,000 km) of the line remained to be built before a direct connection between Europe and the Pacific Ocean could be completed. But, due to Siberia's harsh climate and geological conditions, the line was continued via a southerly section through Manchuria in China. In 1903 this Russian-built Chinese Eastern Railway was put into operation. Lake Baikal, however, was still a barrier: cargo and passengers had to cross the lake by ferry until a rail line around Lake Baikal was put into operation in 1905.

fact: 维特的1895—1897年货币改革确立了俄罗斯金本位：1899年新货币法规规定俄罗斯货币制度以黄金为基础，货币单位卢布含17.424纯金单位（英译文本写作grains）；1897年8月29日法令规定国家银行纸币由国家黄金储备支持并可自由兑换黄金。

sources.title: Money of the Russian Revolution: 1917-1920 (Cambridge Scholars Publishing 样章, Mikhail V. Khodjakov)
sources.quote: The 1895–97 monetary reform of S.Yu.Witte, comprising a series of government initiatives, resulted in 1899 in a new set of monetary regulations stating amongst other things: "The Russian monetary system is based on gold. The Russian state currency unit is the rouble containing 17.424 grains of pure gold". The "gold standard" had been introduced. According to an edict of 29 August 1897, paper banknotes issued by the State Bank – the country's chief issuing institution – were backed by the state gold reserve, and could be freely exchanged for gold.

sources.title: Mr Ruble. The origin and evolution of Russia's national currency | UNESCO (俄罗斯全国委员会)
sources.quote: Sergey Witte's reform (1895–1897) introduced the gold standard, backing the ruble with gold and making credit notes fully convertible to gold.

fact: 根据耶鲁国际金融中心数据编制的指数说明，1865—1917年间约有425家公司先后在圣彼得堡证券交易所挂牌交易；主要行业为银行和铁路公司，石油、公用事业、矿业、保险和钢铁公司提供其余大部分市值，且公司增发的新股与原始股同时挂牌。

sources.title: The Russian Stock Market Before the Revolution (Global Financial Data, 21 March 2018)
sources.quote: Once these issues were designated as scrip, rather than common shares, this left about 425 different companies that traded on the St. Petersburg Stock Exchange between 1865 and 1917, some for a few months, some for the entire 52 years. ... The principal industries were banks and railroads with oil companies, utilities, mining, insurance and iron and steel companies providing most of the capitalization.

fact: 据约翰·穆雷《俄国、波兰与芬兰旅行手册》所载护照规章，依据1864年12月31日意旨，在帝国使领馆取得签证的外国人入境后可凭同一本护照在俄罗斯帝国各地居住和旅行六个月；抵达时须向地方当局出示护照（通常经旅馆老板转交办理）以便登记。

sources.title: Hand-book for Travellers in Russia, Poland, and Finland（穆雷旅行手册，微缩复制本，Wikimedia Commons）
sources.quote: 6.-PASSPORT REGULATIONS. By an idea of the 31st December, 1864, foreigners arriving in Russia, either by sea or by land, with passports duly vised at one of the Imperial Embassies, Legations, or Consulates (in London, 32, Great Winchates-street, City), may reside in any part of Russia, and travel throughout the empire, with the same passport for the term of 6 months. The passport must be exhibited on arrival to the local authorities (through the hotel-keeper, to avoid inconvenience)

fact: 1882年5月15日由沙皇亚历山大三世颁布的对犹太人临时条例（五月法案）限制犹太人在城镇之外重新定居、向其出典或登记城镇外不动产业、并禁止在星期日和基督教主日营业；1887年后教育配额收紧，圣彼得堡与莫斯科的犹太学生比例被限制在3%，这些法律直到1917年仍然有效。

sources.title: May Laws | Wikipedia
sources.quote: Temporary regulations regarding the Jews (also known as May Laws) were residency and business restrictions on Jews in the Russian Empire, proposed by minister Nikolay Pavlovich Ignatyev and enacted by Tsar Alexander III on 15 May [O.S. 3 May] 1882. Originally, intended only as temporary measures, they remained in effect for more than thirty years. ... In 1887, these administrative quotas were tightened down to 10% within the Pale (still double that of Jewish percentage), 5% outside the Pale, except Moscow and St. Petersburg, which were held at 3%. ... Those laws remained in effect until 1917

fact: 1897年俄国第一次现代人口普查记录圣彼得堡（含郊区）总人口1264920人，其中市区1130376人、郊区134544人；该数字被多项研究用作1900年前后首都人口规模的基准。

sources.title: 1897年俄国人口普查圣彼得堡人口研究（澳大利亚国立大学开放研究库收录论文）
sources.quote: The 1897 Census of Imperial Russia was the first and only modern census taken in the Empire. ... Most of the following discussion covers the combined population, which was 1,264,920 of whom 1,130,376 were in the city and 134,544 in the suburbs(T.S.K.b, 1903:VIII).

fact: 圣彼得堡历史图片资料站引用贝特尔《圣彼得堡：工业化与变迁》称，1900年前后圣彼得堡工人每日工作时间可达11.5小时；能进工厂的男工日工资约80戈比、女工约60戈比、童工30—45戈比；维持一个工人家庭可接受生活水平估计每年需600—700卢布，且有轨电车票价昂贵、多数工人步行。

sources.title: St. Petersburg 1900, Photo 38 | Alexander Palace Times
sources.quote: In 1900 workers were at their job up to 11.5 hours a day and most factories requitered their workers to stay on the job this long. ... It has been estimated that the average working family required between 600 - 700 rubles a year to maintain an acceptable standard of living. ... At the bottom of this labouring population were the casual workers. If a factory job were obtained, men were fortunate to draw eighty kopeks a day; women, sixty; juveniles and children, thirty to forty-five. ... Tram travel was expensive and the vast majority of workers walked.

fact: 到1900年，巴库供应了全球约一半的石油；美国标准石油自1870年代的垄断地位受到诺贝尔兄弟与罗斯柴尔德的强烈竞争；诺贝尔自1883年起已控制96公里以上输油管道，1898年巴库地区输油管道达230公里，1901年俄国石油产量约占世界的51%。

fact: 圣彼得堡普梯洛夫工厂在1885—1900年间实现复苏，采取多元化生产策略，除铁轨外还制造机车、货车、火炮和机械；其火炮设计与克虏伯等西欧厂商竞争，1891—1894年三年间工人增加两千人，1903年后大幅扩充军备生产。

sources.title: H-Russia 书评：Jonathan A. Grant, Big Business in Russia: The Putilov Company in Late Imperial Russia, 1868-1917 (H-Net, June 2003)
sources.quote: The period from 1885 to 1900 witnessed a remarkable recovery for the northern giant. Under the direction of N. N. Antsyforov, the Putilov works pursued a strategy of diversified production, including manufacture of not only rails but also locomotives, railroad wagons, artillery, and machine-building. ... The result, Grant argues, was that the factory's workforce grew by two thousand in a mere three years (1891-94), its artillery designs competed successfully with those of major Western European manufacturers such as Krupp's, and by 1903 the firm was able to take on a massive expansion of armaments production
